newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Access sees Australian Q4 CPI rise at zero.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Access sees Australian Q4 CPI rise at zero.

text.p: The Australian consumer price index (CPI) will show zero quarterly growth in the December quarter, forecasters Access Economics said on Monday.

"This figure is solely driven by the move in mortgage interest rates, which will mainly impact in the December quarter," said Access analyst Chris Richardson. "Underlying in the quarter will still be 0.6," he told Reuters.
The Reserve Bank of Australia eased monetary policy on July 31, dropping its target rate for overnight cash to 7.0 percent from 7.5 percent.

Banks immediately announced lower home-loan interest rates -- which are counted in the Australian CPI -- but most of their customers will not get the cut until September, so it will make little difference to quarterly accommodation costs until the December quarter.
Richardson thought the Reserve Bank might exploit the freak December quarter inflation number to drive home a message to the public that price restraint reduces interest rates.
"If the Reserve Bank is going to ram home this result and its significance, then it may well provide a monetary easing as a pay-off, especially if it was already looking for a trigger," he said.
Access forecast a 0.6 percent CPI rise in the September and March quarters and 0.9 percent for the June quarter 1997.
The CPI rose 0.7 percent in the June quarter 1996.
